INTRODUCTION
Zyro Dynamics is committed to securing and maintaining a work environment free from harassment,
exploitation, and intimidation for all employees. While the Company will take every required step to maintain a
harmonious and respectful workplace, employees are also personally responsible for contributing to an
environment in which dignity is respected and upheld.
This Prevention of Sexual Harassment (POSH) Policy has been developed in accordance with the Sexual
Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013, and the rules framed
thereunder. It reflects the Company's firm commitment to preventing sexual harassment and providing a fair,
confidential, and effective mechanism for redressal.
OBJECTIVE
The objective of this policy is to provide protection against sexual harassment at the workplace, to prevent the
occurrence of such harassment, and to provide an accessible and fair mechanism for the redressal of complaints
relating to sexual harassment at Zyro Dynamics.

SCOPE AND APPLICABILITY
This policy applies to all employees of Zyro Dynamics, including full-time, fixed-term, probationary, and
contractual employees, as well as interns, trainees, and third-party personnel working at Zyro Dynamics
premises. It covers conduct at all company workplaces, which includes:
  All Zyro Dynamics offices and premises in India and abroad.
 Any location where work-related activities are being performed, including client sites and co-working spaces.
 Social, business, or professional functions organised by or on behalf of Zyro Dynamics.
 Any location visited by an employee during the course of their work, including while travelling on company
business.
 Digital channels including email, chat applications, social media, and phone communications that are
connected to the workplace relationship.
DEFINITION OF SEXUAL HARASSMENT
Sexual harassment includes any one or more of the following unwelcome acts or behaviour, whether directly or
by implication:
  Physical contact or advances of a sexual nature.
 Demands or requests for sexual favours, whether explicit or implied, in exchange for any work-related
benefit.
 Making sexually coloured remarks, gestures, or jokes.
 Showing pornography or sharing sexually explicit content through any medium.
 Any other unwelcome physical, verbal, or non-verbal conduct of a sexual nature.
The following circumstances, even if not directly sexual in nature, may also amount to sexual harassment when
connected to the workplace relationship:
  An implied or explicit promise of preferential treatment in employment.
 An implied or explicit threat of detrimental treatment or adverse impact on employment status.
 Conduct that creates an intimidating, offensive, or hostile work environment.
 Humiliating treatment that is likely to affect the physical or mental health or safety of the person.
INTERNAL COMPLAINTS COMMITTEE (ICC)
Zyro Dynamics has constituted an Internal Complaints Committee as required under the POSH Act. The ICC is
responsible for receiving, inquiring into, and recommending action on all complaints of sexual harassment.

FILING A COMPLAINT
Any aggrieved person who has experienced sexual harassment may file a complaint with the ICC within 3 months
of the incident or the last incident in a series of incidents. In exceptional circumstances, the ICC may extend this
period by a further 3 months upon written application with reasons.

CONFIDENTIALITY
The identities of the complainant, the respondent, and any witnesses, as well as all proceedings, findings, and
recommendations of the ICC, are strictly confidential. No information shall be communicated to any person other
than those directly involved in the inquiry process or those required to implement the recommendations. Any
breach of confidentiality by any party is itself a disciplinary offence.
PROTECTION FROM RETALIATION
Zyro Dynamics expressly prohibits any form of retaliation against an employee who files a complaint,
participates in an inquiry, or reports a suspected violation under this policy in good faith. Any retaliatory act,
including adverse performance ratings, demotion, transfer, isolation, threats, or termination, will be treated as a
separate and serious disciplinary matter independent of the original complaint.
CONSEQUENCES
On the basis of the ICC's findings and recommendations, the Company may impose the following actions on the
respondent, depending on the gravity of the proven misconduct:
  Written warning with mandatory completion of a sensitisation and inclusion training programme.
 Suspension without pay for a defined period.
 Transfer to a different team, project, or location.
 Withholding of promotion, increment, or other benefits for a specified period.
 Termination of employment with immediate effect.
 Referral to law enforcement where the conduct is found to constitute a criminal offence under applicable
Indian law.
